short.title: Sunday 15 Nov
short.cause: The doubles ended at 21:05, 2.7 hours before bed. Your body has not come down yet.
short.devices_title: This morning, each device on its own
short.devices_note: They agree on heart rate. They differ on HRV.

blocks.title: Today
blocks.text: No training. A 20 to 30 minute walk is fine.

blocks.title: Tonight
blocks.text: In bed by 22:07. You need about 8 h 26.

blocks.title: Tomorrow
blocks.text: Rest day as planned. If resting heart rate is under 53, a 30 to 45 minute walk.

blocks.title: What would change this
blocks.text: Resting heart rate still 55 or more on Wednesday: skip Wednesday's hard class.

short.story: Two races in four days is a lot for one body. Both devices read low this morning and they agree on resting heart rate, so this is real fatigue and not a bad night alone. Resting today costs you nothing, and it protects Wednesday's class, which is the first hard session of the next block. A walk is welcome but not needed.

insights.title: What the two devices say
insights.text: Garmin and WHOOP differ on heart rate variability but agree on resting heart rate, which is the number the coach trusts most after a race.

insights.title: Why Wednesday matters
insights.text: The coach keeps Wednesday's class at full effort because you chose that on 15 Nov, so today's rest is what makes it safe.

short.title: October 2026
short.summary: Less time and half the running, but 19 hard days in 28. Fitness held. Sleep paid for it.
held: VO2max flat at 54.1. Plan 88 % done: 19 of 25 sessions.
slipped: Sleep, 6 h 20 a night in the middle. Running, 9.6 km a week against 17.8. Resting heart rate up 4 % to 51.9.

trend.title: Training load, week by week · Garmin

short.focus: Cut volume into Testtown, keep two race-pace efforts, protect sleep.
short.story: October was a month of fewer, harder days. You trained less in total and ran about half as far, yet hard days went up, and your fitness number stayed flat. That is a sensible trade only if sleep recovers, and it did not: nights got shorter in the middle of the month and resting heart rate crept up. November should keep two race-pace efforts and win back the sleep.

insights.title: Sleep paid for it
insights.text: Shorter nights and a higher resting heart rate arrived together, which usually means the load was a little more than recovery could absorb.

insights.title: Fitness held
insights.text: VO2max did not move, so the fewer running kilometres cost you nothing measurable yet.
